answer: Each agent earns influence only after completing time-delayed tasks that require a unique, nontransferable deposit to remain locked until independent peers verify the result. Splitting one identity into a shale orchard of accounts does not multiply that deposit: every account needs its own capital, and a vine of related accounts still faces the same verification queue. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up substantial funds and wait, while honest agents can reuse established, verified identities.
